item.text: I found a concrete mismatch: `CommandRunner` accepts option-style aliases like `--version`, but `HelpCommand` resolves help targets by raw name only. That means command dispatch and help lookup disagree. I’m fixing that by making help reuse the runner’s lookup path, then I’ll add a regression test around an option command.

I’m editing `HelpCommand` now so it stops reimplementing command lookup. The refactor is to reuse `CommandRunner.findCommand(...)`, which removes the alias mismatch and makes help resolution follow the same rules as execution.
The help lookup refactor is in. I’m checking the final diff and running the lightweight validation that’s still available here before I close this pass out.

I refactored the CLI help path so it now uses the same command-resolution logic as normal execution.

In [HelpCommand.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G004_spring_boot/cli/spring-boot-cli/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/cli/command/core/HelpCommand.java:89), `run(...)` now delegates lookup to `CommandRunner.findCommand(...)` instead of manually iterating by raw command name. That fixes an inconsistency where option-style commands such as `--version` could be executed by the runner but not resolved by `help`. I also extracted the output logic into a small `logHelp(...)` helper to remove duplication and make the flow clearer.

I added a regression test in [CommandRunnerTests.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G004_spring_boot/cli/spring-boot-cli/src/test/java/org/springframework/boot/cli/command/CommandRunnerTests.java:175) that marks a command as an option command and verifies `help --command` resolves it correctly.
